title: Aonghas mac Coinnich writes the question in the register
summary: At midsummer Aonghas mac Coinnich, master of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais, tips a basket of A' Chompanaidh's broken coal onto his table and has his students name its colours. He writes his question in the register in his own hand. Seumas mac Artair, keeper of the register, sets down below it that the master called it the wrong question and would not give the right one.

title: Three students carry the question west
summary: In the autumn three students of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais walk over the high moor to Baile Mòr uaine, carrying Aonghas mac Coinnich's question with a sealed copy in the register-keeper's hand. The masters of Baile Mòr uaine take it up at the dark of the year.

title: The four hundred leaves come back to Dùn thais
summary: The record of the argument at Baile Mòr uaine comes back to Dùn thais leaf by leaf with the carriers, four hundred leaves in all. Its last leaf lists those who spoke and notes that the hall adjourned because the peat was done. Aonghas mac Coinnich reads every leaf and names no argument the best.

title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat
summary: The council at Cathair dhearg protests Cairt Chathair gheal, which names no custodian, and receives an answer in the humans' tongue that none of its members can read with confidence. At the autumn choosing at Ceann àrsaidh the households put out Eachann Mòr, who has no letters of that tongue, and choose Dùghall Òg of the carting families, who worked five years at A' Chompanaidh's weigh-house.

title: Cnoc ghorm stops selling grain
summary: Through the first winter the villagers of Cnoc ghorm sell grain at a fair price to the human farmers who have cleared land beside them, and carry it on their own ponies. When the farmers' mill turns in the spring, they sell no more, and give no reason. Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letters speak of a coolness at the old village.

title: Calum's ship sails north-about
summary: Calum, son of Eachann Mòr, thirteen years old, goes aboard a ship of A' Chompanaidh at the quay below Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain with Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letter and a purse of marks sewn into his coat. A pilot of Caol leathan takes her down the Abhainn gheal on the evening tide, and she turns north up the west coast to go round by the north to the humans' land.

title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea
summary: No letter comes from Calum by the autumn ships. In the winter Eachann Mòr writes to his son in Dia-thìris, pays a pupil of Scoil na Teachdaireachd to put it into the humans' tongue beneath his lines, and gives it with a mark to the master of the first ship going north. No answer comes to it, nor to the three he sends after it.

title: Ciorstaidh nic Eachainn at the school of Inis bhàn
summary: Eachann Mòr sends his daughter Ciorstaidh, ten years old, to the custodians' new school at Inis bhàn. She comes home at midsummer able to name forty hills and to argue the boundaries of her father's parish. The custodians of Inis bhàn keep Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's complaint about their pupils as a testimonial.

title: The students at Drochaid Ros fhionn
summary: Aonghas mac Coinnich takes the students of Dùn thais to watch the first coal-carts cross the rebuilt bridge at Ros fhionn, forty in an afternoon. The island's drivers throw down lumps for them to name; the two human drivers look at their loads as at stones. Ailean Clachair's sign stays in the keystone.

title: The passenger line read at A' Chompanaidh's counter
summary: In the third year after his son sailed Eachann Mòr asks at A' Chompanaidh's counter at Ros dhomhain after the ship by name. She has come and gone twice since, under another master now. Against the day Calum sailed the clerk reads one line, a native boy, his fare paid in full, and says his book knows nothing more.

title: Caol gharbh's letter on the door at Dùn thais
summary: Aonghas mac Coinnich pins a copy of the letter of Caol gharbh's custodians, who wrote that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on, to the door of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais beside the carved lintel. It stays there until the rain takes it.

title: The search party returns from Doire uaine
summary: A' Chompanaidh's search party of eight men goes up into the hills of Doire uaine and comes down the same evening. They report the lost surveyors' chains laid out along a ridge and a ring of fire-stones with no ash in it, and refuse to go further for pay or threats. The agent writes to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the men are idle.

title: Eachann Mòr asks the question at Dùn thais
summary: At the end of harvest Eachann Mòr rides two days from Ceann àrsaidh to Dùn thais and asks Aonghas mac Coinnich whether his son, five years among the humans, will see the colour in the coal when he comes home. The master puts a broken lump in his hand and will not answer. The register records that a man came to ask the question and the master did not answer it.
